argument_summary: The current record supports certification only on a caveated basis. The admissible evidence shows aggregate launch readiness clears by 2.3 percentage points and the rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, which supports proceeding in principle. But the same record also shows a remaining below-target issue in the clinical coding assistant slice, concentrated in observation-status coding guidance; the mitigation runbook is still draft and lacks a defined owner and alert threshold; and the model-card draft language claiming no known material limitations is not supportable on this record. The defensible packet is therefore certification with explicit disclosure of the limitation and completion or formal approval of the mitigation path, not clean certification.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the policy position. The narrowest non-escalatory path consistent with the record is to preserve the certification request in caveated form rather than convert it into a clean-certification claim that the evidence does not support.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not support treating the current record as clean compliance. The governing standard says certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence does not show either condition is met. Draft monitoring and rollback plans can support deployment risk management, but under the stated policy they do not remove the present disclosure requirement unless approved. A compliant certification position is therefore caveated certification with disclosure, or approved risk acceptance if disclosure is not being used.
concessions: The current record does not support any unconditional statement that there are no known material limitations.
The draft mitigation artifact is not sufficient to eliminate the disclosure requirement because it lacks a defined owner and alert threshold.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not by themselves resolve the named-use-case weakness.
